title: Interleave Front and Back
statement:
You get the head of a singly linked list with nodes x₀ → x₁ → … → xₙ₋₁. Rearrange it so the nodes alternate between the front and the back:

x₀ → xₙ₋₁ → x₁ → xₙ₋₂ → x₂ → …

Do it in place, by relinking the existing nodes, and return nothing. The checker reads the list again starting from the same head node. Do not solve it by writing new values into the nodes.

Lists are written as arrays: [8, 3] is 8 → 3. An empty list is null (shown as []).

examples.why: Take from the front, then the back, then the front again. With an odd count the middle node 40 ends up last.
Front 8, back 1, front 3, back 5. With an even count the two middle nodes 3 and 5 finish the list, and 5's next must become null.
With two nodes, "first then last" is the original order. Lists of 0, 1 or 2 nodes do not change.

hints: The order of the back half is reversed in the answer. What linked-list operation gives you the back half in reverse?
Split the list into a front half and a back half. Find the middle with a slow pointer that moves one step while a fast one moves two.
Reverse the back half, cut the link between the halves, then weave: one node from the front half, one from the reversed back half, and repeat.

explain.intuition:
The answer reads the front half forwards and the back half backwards, alternating. A singly linked list cannot walk backwards, but you can reverse the back half once and then walk it forwards. That turns the problem into three small ones you already know: find the middle, reverse a list, merge two lists by alternating.

The fast/slow walk finds the middle without counting first: when fast reaches the end, slow is halfway. Cut the list after slow, so the front half keeps the extra node when the length is odd. The front half is then the same length as the back half or one node longer, which is exactly what the weave needs.
steps: If the list has fewer than 3 nodes, stop: nothing changes.
Find the middle: slow = fast = head; while fast.next and fast.next.next exist, move slow by 1 and fast by 2.
Weave: while second is not null, save a = first.next and b = second.next, link first.next = second and second.next = a, then move first = a, second = b.
pitfalls: Not cutting the list at the middle. The last node of the front half still points into the back half, and the result has a cycle.
Moving the slow pointer one step too far, so the back half is longer than the front. The weave then drops a node or leaves the order wrong for odd lengths.
Returning a new head. The checker reads from the original head node, so the first node must stay first, and the work must happen on the existing nodes.

solutions.title: Detach the tail again and again
solutions.idea: Walk to the second-to-last node, cut the tail off and splice it after the current node. Repeat two nodes further on. Each walk to the tail costs O(n).

solutions.title: Array of nodes, two pointers
solutions.idea: Put every node in an array so you can reach the back in O(1). Then relink from both ends toward the middle.

solutions.title: Middle, reverse, weave
solutions.idea: Find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the back half, and alternate nodes from the two halves.

followups: Undo it: given a woven list, restore the original order in place.
Weave in blocks: two from the front, then two from the back. Which step of the O(1) solution changes?
